newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Banco de Colombia's Q1 net off sharply.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Colombia's Q1 net off sharply.

text.p: Banco de Colombia said its first-quarter net profit came in at a lower-than-expected 6.31 billion pesos against 17.24 billion in the same period last year.
A statement from the bank, Colombia's second largest in terms of assets, suggested that the steep drop in profitability was at least partly due to costs associated with past-due loan provisions.
It said past-due loans, as a percentage of total loans in its consumer credit portfolio, were 6.1 percent.
"Loan loss coverage for the portfolio was 58.9 percent versus 37.2 percent for the first quarter of 1996," the statement said.
"This is consistent with the bank's policies of strengthening its financial structure," the statement added.

For the four quarters to March 31, 1997, the bank reported loan portfolio growth of 18.4 percent in local currency, compared to 25.3 percent for the entire Colombian banking system. It added that Banco de Colombia's total net worth was 449.6 billion pesos as of March 31, up 37.1 percent over the same period last year.

The bank's local stock has dropped sharply since last Friday, when it announced that its talks to form a strategic partnership with Spain's Banco Central Hispano-Americano had collapsed. ((-- Tom Brown, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
